problem: LLM-based robot control is mostly shown in simulation or as end-to-end policies; it is unclear how a reasoning LLM agent behaves when wired to real robot stacks under partial observability, sensor noise, exogenous events and ambiguous commands.
motivation: Bridging abstract plans to real-time control requires maintaining beliefs and reacting to unexpected events. Reasoning-capable tool-using LLMs could plan, act, monitor and recover in one loop, but their reliability and transferability on physical robots are poorly documented.
key_idea: A single plan-act-reflect loop with an OpenAI o3 planner/executor calling one generic act tool over an existing robot skill API, with state snapshots, event polling and a goal-completion critic, transferred across robots by editing only the prompt.
insight: The flexibility comes from separating geometric grounding (classical stack) from language deliberation: moving from Mobipick to Valdemar needed roughly one day of effort, mainly rewriting the domain model, affordances and action catalogue plus rebinding the tool. Qualitative experiments show fragility: irregular event-check calls despite prompt fixes, stale-state placements, nondeterministic charge targets (80/90/100%), and commonsense overriding prompt-encoded affordances (screwdriver vs. drill, which nearly caused a collision). Restricting the LLM to valid API calls gave safe refusals of impossible commands.
method: Router: gpt-5-mini (minimal reasoning) classifies speech-recognised utterances as conversational (sent to chatbot) or actionable (sent to planner/executor).
Planner and Executor (PAE): o3 (low reasoning effort) with a structured prompt; loops reflect -> get state snapshot -> act (one action) -> check events until it stops itself.

Tool interface: reflect (introspection), act(action, params) over {navigate, move_arm, perceive, pick, place, insert, listen, speak}, get semantic environment snapshot, check_events (polled text events).

Prompt structure: domain model, example state, operational rules and safety invariants, affordances, heuristics, action catalogue, few-shot exemplars, and a hand-curated list of past failure patterns.
Goal completion critic: o4-mini reads the execution log and goal, detects 'verbal only' behaviour and requests continuation, but stops when the task is infeasible or blocked.

Semantic state abstraction: symbolic fact generation (at, on, in, arm_posture predicates) from an observation buffer on Mobipick; on Valdemar, geoposition maps to the nearest POI and battery level to okay/low/critical.
Skill bindings return textual success/failure and error traces, with skill docstrings supplied to the model; replanning emerges from the loop rather than being hard-coded.

setting.backbone: OpenAI o3 (planner/executor), gpt-5-mini (router, chatbot), o4-mini (critic), all frozen
setting.observation: symbolic semantic state snapshot (predicates) from perception and telemetry, plus text events; speech input
setting.action_space: high-level parametrised skills (navigate, move_arm, perceive, pick, place, insert, listen, speak) via ROS1-based skill API
setting.simulator: Gazebo (Mobipick sim); real Mobipick; Valdemar tested in simulation
setting.privileged: predefined known locations/POIs and domain model in the prompt; classical perception, grasp and navigation stack; hand-curated failure notes

numbers_note: No quantitative results; the evaluation is qualitative, with seven proof-of-concept experiments and no success rates reported.
results: The agent completed nominal tasks on Mobipick (multimeter into box to table 2, constraint-aware placement, long-horizon 'transport all objects') and Valdemar (waypoint scans, low-battery recharge-and-resume), and it handled ambiguity and e-stop events. It also showed fragility: blind or stale-state placements, inconsistent event checking, nondeterministic stopping criteria, hallucinated alternatives, and no preemption of long actions. No quantitative comparison to baselines is given.
limitations: Purely qualitative proof-of-concept with no quantitative metrics, baselines or repeated-trial statistics; Valdemar only in simulation
Polling-based event handling cannot preempt long-running actions; remote LLM inference adds unmeasured cost, latency and internet dependence
Prompt sensitivity and labour-intensive domain modelling; safety constraints must be repeated redundantly yet are still occasionally violated
builds_on: Mobipick physics-based robot stack (Lima et al. 2023)
